plan.title: Whole-blood case/control cohort: subgroup discovery beyond diagnosis
plan.analytical_narrative: The 120-sample whole-blood cohort (60 case, 60 control, single batch, raw Salmon gene counts, 12000 genes) is asked whether it holds sample subgroups beyond the case/control label. The plan follows the grounded bulk-RNA-seq clustering procedure: (1) sample-structure QC with a blind variance-stabilizing transform, PCA and a Euclidean sample-distance heatmap to see the gross structure and flag outliers or a technical driver of variance before any clustering; (2) a minimal filterByExpr low-count filter so genes with no real signal do not dilute variance-based gene selection; (3) consensus clustering of the samples with ConsensusClusterPlus on the top 2000 most-variable genes after the blind VST, using hierarchical clustering with 1-minus-Pearson-correlation distance and average linkage, 1000 resamples at 80% item subsampling, screening k=2..8, with k chosen from the consensus CDF delta-area and confirmed by the proportion of ambiguous clustering (PAC) - not from the embedding alone; (4) a PCA/UMAP visualization step that is explicitly descriptive only (no cluster claims from the embedding itself, per the grounded rule that UMAP/t-SNE give a picture, not a distance or cluster claim); (5) a confounding check that cross-tabulates the chosen clusters against case/control status, library size, and any other metadata columns available, because whole blood is highly sensitive to cell-composition shifts and a 'subgroup' that is actually a proportion of granulocytes/lymphocytes is a different finding than a disease subtype; (6) an MCP-counter immune/stromal deconvolution on the same samples (log2-CPM input) so that a discovered cluster structure can be checked against cell-composition and reported honestly as either a distinct molecular subgroup or a restatement of blood cell composition; (7) a consolidated report stating the input transform, gene count, distance/linkage, resampling parameters, the k evidence (CDF/delta-area/PAC), each sample's cluster with its item consensus, cluster consensus, the confounder cross-tabs, and the explicit caution that consensus clustering finds apparent structure even in unstructured data, so any subgroup found here is a hypothesis pending independent or external validation.

PCA and UMAP as descriptive visualization only, no cluster claims from embedding
Cluster stability report: consensus CDF, delta-area, PAC, item/cluster consensus, cross-tab vs case/control label, library size, and any available technical covariates
